unit: Unit 12: Everyday Life with Your Computer
title: Reading and Saving PDFs
drDigitalIntro:
In Unit 4 you learned how to download files — PDFs are one of the most common things you will download.

PDFs look identical on every device, which makes them perfect for forms, receipts, invoices, and instruction manuals.

To open a PDF from the internet:
1. Click a PDF link and your browser will usually open it straight away in a built-in viewer.
2. Use the zoom controls (usually a + and - button at the top) to enlarge small print.
3. Scroll through the pages just as you would a web page.

To save a PDF to your computer:
1. Click the download arrow in the browser viewer's toolbar.
2. The file goes to your Downloads folder automatically.
3. Open your Files or Finder app, go to Downloads, and double-click the PDF to open it later.

To create a PDF from anything you can print:
1. Press Ctrl+P (or Command+P on a Mac) to open the Print window.
2. In the Printer dropdown, choose 'Save as PDF' or 'Microsoft Print to PDF'.
3. Click Save and choose where to put the file.

Tip: PDFs from your bank, insurance company, or doctor are important — save them in a named folder so you can find them again.
drDigitalSuccess: You know how to open, read, and save PDFs! They are one of the most useful file types you will come across every day.
drDigitalHint: Find a PDF link online and click it — your browser will open it. Look for the download arrow in the viewer to save a copy.
